method: Camel: std::profile(report=true,json=...,top=0) on the generated train_step.cml; operator rows of the 16-step run minus the same run's steps=0 pre/post; mean per step. The layout/copy row is only operators whose whole job is a layout change or an allocation; copies and allocations inside a matmul or elementwise kernel are inside that operator's row and are not separable with today's operator-boundary timer. PyTorch: torch.profiler FunctionEvent self time over 3 steps, grouped by the same categories; the Adam section is kept whole under optimizer because eager Adam is a chain of elementwise kernels. The two profilers add different overhead (Camel step wall 3484 ms vs timed 3145 ms, +11%; naive +22%, compiled +11%), so compare shares and the excess, not absolute totals across tools.

build.note: The canonical column was measured before the BLAS change; the library column after CAMEL_TENSOR_BLAS became the default. The sweep's build is b2e4abd0e50d; the final tree (one comment and a JSON newline later) rebuilds to 97346a9d8921 and runs the same code path.

commands.camel_canonical: camel -t 1 --block-limit 8192 train_step.cml 'std::profile(report=true,json="/tmp/prof.json",top=0)' std::jit --arg bench=true --arg init_dir=<init> --arg final_dir=
commands.camel_library: camel -t 1 --block-limit 8192 train_step.cml tensor::fuse 'std::profile(report=true,json="/tmp/prof.json",top=0)' std::jit --arg bench=true --arg init_dir=<init> --arg final_dir=

matmul.detail: tensor:matmul 806.4 ms (17 calls/step); tensor:matmul_grad_lhs 1167.9 ms + tensor:matmul_grad_rhs 848.8 ms (17 each)

library_path.detail: forward tensor:matmul 929.8 ms vs 806.4 canonical (+123.4 ms, 15%); the grad rows are unchanged in code and their -72 ms here is run-to-run load, not the library. The pass marks tensor:matmul only; autodiff creates matmul_grad_lhs/rhs after the pass, so those 2016.7 ms stay on the canonical kernel.
library_path.note: The library GEMM is not a step-level win at this shape: the timed median is 3337 ms against 3145 ms canonical (+6%), and OpenBLAS is slower on the model's many batched forward products. It never sees the backward matmuls.

gap.explanation: Matmul owns the profiled gap almost exactly: 2823.1 - 1982.6 = 840.5 ms of the 846.9 ms total. Camel's Adam is 407 ms cheaper and its elementwise/reduction/layout excess is partly offset by that, so the other categories nearly cancel.

re_measured_sweep_one_thread.note: The before/after medians are not a controlled A/B: the cell's load went from 12 to 31 and one Camel round took 4309 ms. The paired profile's timed median is 3145 ms canonical against 3337 ms with the library (+6%); torch.compile moved 1.4%. The gap remains and is wider by median (48% vs 33%) because of the host, not because the library is 13% slower.
